                      [32m'created: 2026-05-15, last updated: 2026-07-27, [Read more](https://typesense.org/docs/30.2/api/stemming.html)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Stemming is a technique that helps handle variations of words during search.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When stemming is enabled, a search for one form of a word will also match other grammatical forms of that word.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Then upload it using the stemming dictionary API:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-09, [Read more](https://docs-python.ru/other/polnotekstovyi-poisk-s-typesense/sinonimy-stopwords-stemming-ruchnaya-nastroi-ka-vy/)\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Stemming помогает обрабатывать грамматические формы слова.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Документация Typesense описывает stemming как технику, при которой поиск по одной форме слова может находить другие формы; basic stemming использует Snowball stemmer, а язык определяется через `locale` поля.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. **Addressing French Accents and Transliteration** - **Normalization:** - Store a normalized version of text without accents (e.g., "é" → "e") in additional fields or as a searchable attribute.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Use this normalized field for search matching to make accent-insensitive searches.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Transliteration:** - For French accents, consider preprocessing content to generate both accented and unaccented versions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- During indexing, include unaccented variants in separate fields, enabling searches that ignore accents.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'4.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'5. **Implementation Workflow** - **Indexing:** - Detect and store language of each article.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Generate normalized (accentless) versions of content.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Store all variants in the schema.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Query Handling:** - Detect query language.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Accent Fold (Search Normaliser) — Gera Tools\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-06, last updated: 2026-07-29, [Read more](https://geratools.com/accent-fold)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Accent folding normalises text so that searches match regardless of accents and special letters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It is the standard preprocessing step behind diacritic-insensitive search, where café and cafe are treated as identical.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## How it works\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Two stages produce a clean ASCII key:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Expand special letters and ligatures that have no combining mark:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ß → ss æ → ae œ → oe ø → o ð → d þ → th ł → l\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Normalise to NFD and delete combining marks (U+0300–U+036F):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'é → e ñ → n ü → u\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(optionally) lowercase the whole string\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Doing the ligature expansion before the NFD strip ensures characters that NFD cannot decompose still become plain ASCII.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Apply the same pipeline to both your search index and the incoming query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Input|Folded output|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Always fold both sides.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Text Normalization: Unicode Forms, Case Folding & Whitespace ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-03-17, last updated: 2026-06-25, [Read more](https://mbrenndoerfer.com/writing/text-normalization-unicode-nlp)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The standard approach uses NFD normalization followed by filtering.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The algorithm has an elegant three-step structure: decompose the text so that every accent becomes a separate combining mark, filter out all combining marks, then recompose the remaining characters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This works because NFD guarantees that every diacritical mark is represented as an explicit code point with Unicode category "Mn" (Mark, Nonspacing), making filtering straightforward.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For search applications, you might want to match both forms.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For translation or language understanding, preserving diacritics is essential.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A practical approach is to build a search index that contains both the original and the diacritic-stripped form of each document, so that queries with or without accents both retrieve relevant results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is sometimes called "accent folding" in search engine terminology.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Unicode normalization forms**: NFC composes, NFD decomposes, NFKC and NFKD add compatibility mappings\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Case folding**: Use `casefold()` for case-insensitive comparison, not `lower()`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Diacritic handling**: NFD decomposition plus filtering removes accents cleanly and without a lookup table'[39m

                content: [32m"const express = require('express');\n"[39m +
                  [32m"const Typesense = require('typesense');\n"[39m +
                  [32m"const fs = require('fs');\n"[39m +
                  [32m"const path = require('path');\n"[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'const app = express();\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Read API key from file\n'[39m +
                  [32m"const apiKey = fs.readFileSync('/etc/typesense-api-key', 'utf8').trim();\n"[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Initialize Typesense client\n'[39m +
                  [32m'const client = new Typesense.Client({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  nodes: [{\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    host: '127.0.0.1',\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    port: '8108',\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    protocol: 'http'\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  }],\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  apiKey: apiKey,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  connectionTimeoutSeconds: 5\n'[39m +
                  [32m'});\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Setup Typesense collection and index catalog data\n'[39m +
                  [32m'async function initTypesense() {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const schema = {\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    name: 'catalog',\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    fields: [\n'[39m +
                  [32m"      { name: 'id', type: 'string' },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"      { name: 'name_en', type: 'string', locale: 'en', stem: true },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"      { name: 'name_fr', type: 'string', locale: 'fr', stem: true },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"      { name: 'name_de', type: 'string', locale: 'de', stem: true }\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    ]\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  try {\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    console.log('Checking if catalog collection exists...');\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    await client.collections('catalog').delete();\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    console.log('Existing catalog collection deleted.');\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  } catch (err) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    // Collection did not exist, which is fine\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m"  console.log('Creating catalog collection...');\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  await client.collections().create(schema);\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  // Create synonyms for morphological matching across different languages\n'[39m +

                  [32m'  const synonyms = [\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    // English\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-baking', synonyms: ['baking', 'bake'] },\n"[39m +

                  [32m"    { id: 'en-finishing', synonyms: ['finishing', 'finish'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-carving', synonyms: ['carving', 'carve'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-painting', synonyms: ['painting', 'paint'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-basics', synonyms: ['basics', 'basic'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-classes', synonyms: ['classes', 'class'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-workshops', synonyms: ['workshops', 'workshop'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    // French\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-finir', synonyms: ['finir', 'finissons', 'finis'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-sauce', synonyms: ['sauce', 'sauces'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-base', synonyms: ['base', 'bases'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-naive', synonyms: ['naïve', 'naïf', 'naive', 'naif'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-pain', synonyms: ['pain', 'pains'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-peinture', synonyms: ['peinture', 'peindre'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-emaillage', synonyms: ['émaillage', 'émailler', 'emaillage', 'emailler'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-sculpture', synonyms: ['sculpture', 'sculpter'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    // German\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-schnitzen', synonyms: ['schnitzens', 'schnitzen', 'Schnitzens'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-sauce', synonyms: ['Saucen', 'Sauce', 'saucen', 'sauce'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-verfeinern', synonyms: ['verfeinern', 'verfeinert'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-backkurs', synonyms: ['backkurs', 'backen', 'Backkurs'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-glasurkurs', synonyms: ['glasurkurs', 'glasur', 'Glasurkurs', 'Glasur'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-volksmalerei', synonyms: ['volksmalerei', 'malerei', 'Volksmalerei', 'Malerei'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-beschilderung', synonyms: ['beschilderung', 'schild', 'Beschilderung', 'Schild'] }\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  ];\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  for (const syn of synonyms) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    await client.collections('catalog').synonyms().upsert(syn.id, { synonyms: syn.synonyms });\n"[39m +

                  [32m'}\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Search endpoint\n'[39m +
                  [32m"app.get('/api/search', async (req, res) => {\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  const q = req.query.q;\n'[39m +

                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +

                  [32m"    const searchResults = await client.collections('catalog').documents().search({\n"[39m +
                  [32m'      q: q.trim(),\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      query_by: `name_${lang}`\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const hits = searchResults.hits.map(hit => ({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      id: hit.document.id,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      name: hit.document[`name_${lang}`]\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }));\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    return res.json({ hits });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } catch (err) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    console.error('Search error:', err);\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    return res.status(500).json({ error: 'Search failed' });\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'});\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Search page\n'[39m +
                  [32m"app.get('/', (req, res) => {\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  const html = `<!DOCTYPE html>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'<html lang="en">\n'[39m +
                  [32m'<head>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <meta charset="UTF-8">\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <title>Multilingual Catalog Search</title>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <style>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    body {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      font-family: Arial, sans-serif;\n'[39m +

                  [32m'    #search-input {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      width: 300px;\n'[39m +

                  [32m'    #language-select {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      padding: 8px;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      font-size: 16px;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    #results {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      margin-top: 20px;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      padding-left: 20px;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    .result-item {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      margin-bottom: 8px;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      font-size: 18px;\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  </style>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'</head>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'<body>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <h1>Catalog Search</h1>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <div>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    <select id="language-select">\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      <option value="en" selected>English</option>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      <option value="fr">French</option>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      <option value="de">German</option>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    </select>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    <input id="search-input" type="text" placeholder="Search...">\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  </div>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  \n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <ul id="results"></ul>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <script>\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    const langSelect = document.getElementById('language-select');\n"[39m +

                  [32m"    const resultsList = document.getElementById('results');\n"[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    async function performSearch() {\n'[39m +

                  [32m'        \n'[39m +

            [32m'CRITICAL REQUIREMENTS FOR USING THIS TOOL:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Directory Verification:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use listFiles to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - For example, before running "mkdir foo/bar", first use listFiles to check that "foo" exists and is the intended parent directory\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. Command Execution:\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Examples of proper quoting:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands\n'[39m +

            [32m'- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'</example>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +

            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +

            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.                       [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. **Addressing French Accents and Transliteration** - **Normalization:** - Store a normalized version of text without accents (e.g., "é" → "e") in additional fields or as a searchable attribute.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Accent Fold (Search Normaliser) — Gera Tools\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-06-06, last updated: 2026-07-29, [Read more](https://geratools.com/accent-fold)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Accent folding normalises text so that searches match regardless of accents and special letters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It is the standard preprocessing step behind diacritic-insensitive search, where café and cafe are treated as identical.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## How it works\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Two stages produce a clean ASCII key:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Expand special letters and ligatures that have no combining mark:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'ß → ss æ → ae œ → oe ø → o ð → d þ → th ł → l\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Normalise to NFD and delete combining marks (U+0300–U+036F):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'é → e ñ → n ü → u\n'[39m +
                      [32m'(optionally) lowercase the whole string\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Doing the ligature expansion before the NFD strip ensures characters that NFD cannot decompose still become plain ASCII.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Apply the same pipeline to both your search index and the incoming query.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Input|Folded output|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Always fold both sides.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Text Normalization: Unicode Forms, Case Folding & Whitespace ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-03-17, last updated: 2026-06-25, [Read more](https://mbrenndoerfer.com/writing/text-normalization-unicode-nlp)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The standard approach uses NFD normalization followed by filtering.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The algorithm has an elegant three-step structure: decompose the text so that every accent becomes a separate combining mark, filter out all combining marks, then recompose the remaining characters.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This works because NFD guarantees that every diacritical mark is represented as an explicit code point with Unicode category "Mn" (Mark, Nonspacing), making filtering straightforward.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For search applications, you might want to match both forms.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For translation or language understanding, preserving diacritics is essential.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A practical approach is to build a search index that contains both the original and the diacritic-stripped form of each document, so that queries with or without accents both retrieve relevant results.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is sometimes called "accent folding" in search engine terminology.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Unicode normalization forms**: NFC composes, NFD decomposes, NFKC and NFKD add compatibility mappings\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- **Diacritic handling**: NFD decomposition plus filtering removes accents cleanly and without a lookup table'[39m

                content: [32m"const express = require('express');\n"[39m +
                  [32m"const Typesense = require('typesense');\n"[39m +
                  [32m"const fs = require('fs');\n"[39m +
                  [32m"const path = require('path');\n"[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'const app = express();\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Read API key from file\n'[39m +
                  [32m"const apiKey = fs.readFileSync('/etc/typesense-api-key', 'utf8').trim();\n"[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Initialize Typesense client\n'[39m +
                  [32m'const client = new Typesense.Client({\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  nodes: [{\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    host: '127.0.0.1',\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    port: '8108',\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    protocol: 'http'\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  }],\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  apiKey: apiKey,\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  connectionTimeoutSeconds: 5\n'[39m +
                  [32m'});\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Setup Typesense collection and index catalog data\n'[39m +
                  [32m'async function initTypesense() {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  const schema = {\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    name: 'catalog',\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    fields: [\n'[39m +
                  [32m"      { name: 'id', type: 'string' },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"      { name: 'name_en', type: 'string', locale: 'en', stem: true },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"      { name: 'name_fr', type: 'string', locale: 'fr', stem: true },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"      { name: 'name_de', type: 'string', locale: 'de', stem: true }\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    ]\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  };\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  try {\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    console.log('Checking if catalog collection exists...');\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    await client.collections('catalog').delete();\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    console.log('Existing catalog collection deleted.');\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  } catch (err) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    // Collection did not exist, which is fine\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m"  console.log('Creating catalog collection...');\n"[39m +

                  [32m"    { id: 'en-carving', synonyms: ['carving', 'carve'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-painting', synonyms: ['painting', 'paint'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-basics', synonyms: ['basics', 'basic'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-classes', synonyms: ['classes', 'class'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'en-workshops', synonyms: ['workshops', 'workshop'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    // French\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-finir', synonyms: ['finir', 'finissons', 'finis'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-sauce', synonyms: ['sauce', 'sauces'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-base', synonyms: ['base', 'bases'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-naive', synonyms: ['naïve', 'naïf', 'naive', 'naif'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-pain', synonyms: ['pain', 'pains'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-peinture', synonyms: ['peinture', 'peindre'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-emaillage', synonyms: ['émaillage', 'émailler', 'emaillage', 'emailler'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'fr-sculpture', synonyms: ['sculpture', 'sculpter'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m'    // German\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-schnitzen', synonyms: ['schnitzens', 'schnitzen', 'Schnitzens'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-sauce', synonyms: ['Saucen', 'Sauce', 'saucen', 'sauce'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-verfeinern', synonyms: ['verfeinern', 'verfeinert'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-backkurs', synonyms: ['backkurs', 'backen', 'Backkurs'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-glasurkurs', synonyms: ['glasurkurs', 'glasur', 'Glasurkurs', 'Glasur'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-volksmalerei', synonyms: ['volksmalerei', 'malerei', 'Volksmalerei', 'Malerei'] },\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    { id: 'de-beschilderung', synonyms: ['beschilderung', 'schild', 'Beschilderung', 'Schild'] }\n"[39m +

                  [32m'  for (const syn of synonyms) {\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Search endpoint\n'[39m +
                  [32m"app.get('/api/search', async (req, res) => {\n"[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    const hits = searchResults.hits.map(hit => ({\n'[39m +

                  [32m'      name: hit.document[`name_${lang}`]\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    }));\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    return res.json({ hits });\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  } catch (err) {\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    console.error('Search error:', err);\n"[39m +
                  [32m"    return res.status(500).json({ error: 'Search failed' });\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  }\n'[39m +
                  [32m'});\n'[39m +
                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'// Search page\n'[39m +
                  [32m"app.get('/', (req, res) => {\n"[39m +
                  [32m'  const html = `<!DOCTYPE html>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'<html lang="en">\n'[39m +
                  [32m'<head>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <meta charset="UTF-8">\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <title>Multilingual Catalog Search</title>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <style>\n'[39m +

                  [32m'    #results {\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      margin-top: 20px;\n'[39m +

                  [32m'  </style>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'</head>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'<body>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <h1>Catalog Search</h1>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <div>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    <select id="language-select">\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      <option value="en" selected>English</option>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      <option value="fr">French</option>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'      <option value="de">German</option>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    </select>\n'[39m +
                  [32m'    <input id="search-input" type="text" placeholder="Search...">\n'[39m +

                  [32m'\n'[39m +
                  [32m'  <script>\n'[39m +
                  [32m"    const langSelect = document.getElementById('language-select');\n"[39m +

          description: [32m'Executes a given bash command in a persistent shell session with optional timeout, ensuring proper handling and security measures.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Directory Verification:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use listFiles to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - For example, before running "mkdir foo/bar", first use listFiles to check that "foo" exists and is the intended parent directory\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. Command Execution:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes (e.g., cd "path with spaces/file.txt")\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Examples of proper quoting:\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - cd "/Users/name/My Documents" (correct)\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - cd /Users/name/My Documents (incorrect - will fail)\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - python "/path/with spaces/script.py" (correct)\n'[39m +
            [32m'     - python /path/with spaces/script.py (incorrect - will fail)\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - After ensuring proper quoting, execute the command.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Capture the output of the command.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple executeCommand tool calls in a single message. For example, if you need to run "git status" and "git diff", send a single message with two executeCommand tool calls in parallel.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`). For instance, if one operation must complete before another starts (like mkdir before cp, Write before executeCommand for git operations, or git add before git commit), run these operations sequentially instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +
            [32m'  - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings)\n'[39m +
            [32m"- You shall avoid use the markdown code block syntax (backtick, '`') in your command, as it will be interpreted as a command substitution.\n"[39m +

You must also consider if the command you need to run should be executed in a specific directory rather than the current working directory, and properly set the `cwd` if necessary.\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- CRITICAL: Always create NEW commits rather than amending, unless the user explicitly requests a git amend. When a pre-commit hook fails, the commit did NOT happen  — so --amend would modify the PREVIOUS commit, which may result in destroying work or losing previous changes. Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- When staging files, prefer adding specific files by name rather than using "git add -A" or "git add .", which can accidentally include sensitive files (.env, credentials) or large binaries\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER commit changes unless the user explicitly asks you to. It is VERY IMPORTANT to only commit when explicitly asked, otherwise the user will feel that you are being too proactive\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel, each using the executeCommand tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git status command to see all untracked files. IMPORTANT: Never use the -uall flag as it can cause memory issues on large repos.\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed.\n'[39m +
            [32m"  - Run a git log command to see recent commit messages, so that you can follow this repository's commit message style.\n"[39m +
            [32m'2. Analyze all staged changes (both previously staged and newly added) and draft a commit message:\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'   Note: Replace <Share URL> with the Share URL from system information if available. If not available, omit the " | [Task](...)" part.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands\n'[39m +
            [32m'- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit\n'[39m +
            [32m'- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:\n'[39m +
            [32m'<example>\n'[39m +
            [32m`git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'\n`[39m +

            [32m'EOF\n'[39m +
            [32m')"\n'[39m +
            [32m'</example>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)\n'[39m +

          description: [32m'Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks autonomously.\n'[39m +
            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### reviewer\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to perform code reviews and leave inline comments.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent can analyze code and create review comments on specific lines.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "review the code in src/auth"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "add review comments to this file"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "check this code and leave feedback"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +
            [32m'If the task stops without submitting the result, it will return an error message.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you want to read a specific file path, use the readFile or globFiles tool instead of the newTask tool, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If you are searching for a specific class definition like "class Foo", use the globFiles tool instead, to find the match more quickly\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Usage notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Launch multiple agents tools concurrently whenever possible to maximize performance; to do that, use a single message with multiple tool uses\n'[39m +
            [32m'2. When the agent is done, it will return a single message back to you. The result returned by the agent is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
